events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 2.8 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Pacific Ocean Coast. * WHEN...Through 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.0 ft above normal (7.8 ft MLLW) at 8:48 AM Sunday, 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding expected. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 4 AM Sunday to 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from 4 AM PST Tuesday through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Morning high tides will be on the increase this upcoming week. Highest tides will be Tuesday through Thursday, peaking Wednesday. Daily high tides each morning on Tuesday through Thursday will reach 7.9-8.2 feet, likely re- breaking the all time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday could bring notably higher surf beginning on Thursday. Uncertainty remains in exact surf heights at this time, but look to be 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides and storm surge will cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Humboldt Bay Coast. Up to 1.5 to 2.0 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 9.5 and 9.8 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf with storm surge may cause moderate flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood/Mendocino Coast. Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM to noon PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Monday afternoon through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 9:44 AM at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms/sections of highway 101 Shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public..

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.

Coastal Areas.

Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the
time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7
AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday.

including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp
increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking
waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing
beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks
to be around 5-8 feet.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.0 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding with up to 2.8 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday night to midnight PST Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 9:25 AM Monday, 2.6 ft above normal (8.4 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.8 ft above normal (8.6 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.6 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) are expected to bring up to 2.4 ft of inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways on Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, higher than normal astronomical tides (King Tides) combined with storm surge from large surf are expected to bring up to 3.1 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 7 AM to 4 PM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. This event is expected see similar impacts to what occurred on January 3rd, 2026. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. This is especially so for Tuesday and Wednesday as storm activity brings large breaking surf heights of 23 to 28 ft and adds storm surge to the water levels. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM Monday, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

Up to one foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Thursday afternoon during periods of high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion may occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Expect continued increases in high tide water levels through the coming work week with the tide peaking on Wednesday. Prepare now and pay attention to official guidance on shelters and or resources available to the public.

location.region: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 23 at 3:42PM ChST until November 26 at 3:00PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce
a high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs. Surf along
east-facing reefs will also be elevated with the rip current
risk along north-facing reefs also elevated.
weather.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.
weather.areaDesc: Guam; Rota; Tinian; Saipan

For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Monday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday, reaching 7.9-8.3 feet, likely re-breaking the all- time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 3-5 feet through Wednesday, but an incoming swell Wednesday into Thursday will bring a sharp increase to the surf by Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with sets up to 10 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf then moderates some into Friday, but still looks to be around 5-8 feet.

location.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas; Orange County Coastal

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along Bogue Banks beaches, Bogue Sound, the Newport and White Oak Rivers, and adjacent tidal creeks, and areas in North Topsail Beach, the lower New River, and adjacent tidal creeks. * WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday evening. * IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of vehicles will be possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to bring nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across the watch area with minor to locally moderate impacts forecast on Wednesday. The worst impacts are currently forecast with the morning high tide cycle on Thursday.

weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

* WHAT...Tidal overflow flooding.

* WHERE...Clatsop County Coast.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PST Thursday during periods of high tide.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal
overflow flooding of low-lying areas is expected due to high
tides. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert for
rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

will be 11.2 feet at Tuesday November 24th at 1153 AM PST, 11.7
feet Wednesday November 25th at 1238 PM PST, and 11.6 feet
Thursday November 26th at 125 PM PST.

property.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...From Tuesday evening through late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 1-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6-8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM Tuesday to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM on Tuesday to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak Tuesday through Wednesday at 7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

location.region: San Diego County Coastal Areas

weather.description:

possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal

* WHERE...Ocean, Atlantic, Coastal Atlantic, Coastal Ocean and
Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, widespread roadway flooding occurs in
coastal and bayside communities and along inland tidal

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Areas along Bogue Banks beaches, Bogue Sound, the Newport and White Oak Rivers, and adjacent tidal creeks, and areas in North Topsail Beach, the lower New River, and adjacent tidal creeks. * WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 3 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of vehicles will be possible. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the morning hours each day this week. This is forecast to bring nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across the watch area with minor to locally moderate impacts forecast on Wednesday. The worst impacts are currently forecast with the morning high tide cycle on Thursday.

sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides, combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to 2.8 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...From 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at 11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.

location.region: South Central Oregon Coast; Curry County Coast

OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF
OAHU...

.A large to extra large, long-period north- northwest swell build
down the island chain on Tuesday. While the source low aimed its
peak swell energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at
Hawaii to see surf build to warning levels during the day on
Tuesday before subsiding on Wednesday ahead of an even larger
north-northwest swell on Wednesday night into Thursday.

12 to 16 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along
Oahu's east-facing shores.

* WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu,
Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Tuesday to 6 AM HST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous.
weather.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Significant coastal flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. * WHERE...San Francisco County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday night to midnight PST Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW) at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49 AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: A disturbance will pass near or south of the local area late Tuesday and into Wednesday. Saturated soils from recent heavy rainfall will increase the risk of additional flooding across portions of central Florida. Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are forecast with localized higher totals of 3 to 4 inches possible. * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including, Indian River, Martin, Saint Lucie, Brevard, and Okeechobee counties. * WHEN...From late Tuesday night through late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are forecast with localized higher amounts of 3 to 4 inches. Heavy rainfall over saturated soils may lead to flooding. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
A disturbance will pass near or south of the local area late Tuesday
and into Wednesday. Saturated soils from recent heavy rainfall will
increase the risk of additional flooding across portions of central
Florida. Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are forecast with
localized higher totals of 3 to 4 inches possible.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of east central Florida, including, Indian River,
Martin, Saint Lucie, Brevard, and Okeechobee counties.

* WHEN...From late Tuesday night through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are forecast with localized
higher amounts of 3 to 4 inches. Heavy rainfall over saturated
soils may lead to flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

events.title: Rip Current Statement
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas. * WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce elevated surf with a high risk of rip currents along east-facing reefs at least through Thursday afternoon. Another trade-wind surge is possible later this week, potentially continuining the threat of rip currents beyond Thursday.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...East facing reefs of the Marianas.

* WHEN...Through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from
shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A trade-wind swell will continue to produce

weather.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. If caught in a rip current,
relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the shore
and call or wave for help.

weather.description:

* WHEN...From 11 PM Tuesday to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means sub-freezing temperatures are imminent or
highly likely. These conditions will kill crops and other sensitive
vegetation.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold. To prevent
freezing and possible bursting of outdoor water pipes they should be
wrapped, drained, or allowed to drip slowly. Those that have
in-ground sprinkler systems should drain them and cover above-ground
pipes to protect them from freezing.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to 9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning through Thursday morning. * IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long Beach). * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will likely peak between 7am and 11am. An upgrade to a Coastal Flood Warning would likely come by Tuesday. Coastal Flood and High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of the respective warnings if they are issued.

location.region: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 4:04PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to
9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday
morning through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and
Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high
tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long
Beach).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. An upgrade to a Coastal
Flood Warning would likely come by Tuesday. Coastal Flood and
High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of
the respective warnings if they are issued.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5 to 10 feet with dangerous rip currents. Conditions will be worse west of Point Conception, including Jalama Beach with large breaking waves of 15 to 20 feet and moderate to significant coastal flooding possible. * WHERE...Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast and Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon PST Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to noon PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely. Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this evening to 3 AM EST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 1 AM to 7 PM EST Wednesday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

weather.description:

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents expected.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6 to 8 feet.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Duval County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 1 AM EST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late
Wednesday night. For the High Surf Advisory, from 11 PM this
evening to 3 AM EST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
from 1 AM to 7 PM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline erosion or damage may occur. events.description: * WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and seas 5 to 7 ft expected. * WHERE...Offshore Gulf waters from the Walton-Okaloosa County line to the Ochlockonee River from 20 to 60 nautical miles out, Nearshore Gulf waters from the Ochlockonee River to the Suwannee River out 20 nautical miles, Coastal waters from Mexico Beach to Okaloosa Walton County Line FL out 20 NM, Coastal waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL out 20 NM, and Coastal Waters From Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola Fl out to 20 Nm. * WHEN...From 8 PM EST /7 PM CST/ this evening to 8 PM EST /7 PM CST/ Wednesday. * IMPACTS...A Small Craft Advisory means that wind speeds of 20 to 33 knots, or seas of 7 feet or greater, are expected to produce hazardous conditions for small craft. These hazardous conditions may result in poor vessel handling and steering response, broaching, overturned dinghies and kayaks, slips and falls on slippery decks, rub damage along docks and seawalls, and dragging anchors.

events.title: Coastal Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and large surf may cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood Coast. Up to 2.5 foot of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on Wednesday and 11:56 AM on Thursday at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. These impacts will include, but not limited to, roadways and houses in King Salmon and the Arcata bottoms. This may also include highway 101 near College of the Redwoods and Hwy 255 near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The water levels from this are expected to exceed the water levels seen in January of 2026 that caused significant flooding in King Salmon.

events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 6- 8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches. * WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at 7.9- 8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west- facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's high tide.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...From this evening through late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.headline: Freeze Warning issued November 24 at 11:03AM CST until November 25 at 9:00AM CST by NWS Fort Worth TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures as low as 25 degrees expected.

* WHERE...Western portions of north central Texas.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and

events.description: * WHAT...High risk of life-threatening rip currents. * WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline, from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In the U.S. Virgin Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St. Thomas, St. John and adjacent islands. * WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to return to safety.

location.region: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra; St.Thomas...St. John.. and Adjacent Islands

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 24 at 9:33PM AST until November 25 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High risk of life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline,
from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In the U.S.
Virgin Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St.
Thomas, St. John and adjacent islands.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Coastal Flagler County. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 PM EST Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Coastal Flagler

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 24 at 8:18PM EST until November 26 at 4:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 PM EST
Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through late
Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Statement
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3 to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Statement, isolated minor coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Wednesday. For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday afternoon. For the Coastal Flood Statement, through late tonight. * IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued November 24 at 5:58PM CST until November 25 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Statement,
isolated minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Wednesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Wednesday afternoon.
For the Coastal Flood Statement, through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could
be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees and power lines.

weather.instruction:

the onset of winds.

are relative to nearby trees and powerlines.

generator, ensure you have enough fuel. Ensure you have batteries,
flashlights, and a way to maintain a safe body temperature if you
were to lose heating and cooling.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

6 feet expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood
Advisory, up to one foot of inundation above ground level
expected along shorelines and tidal waterways (10.2 to 10.4 feet
Mean Lower Low Water at Fort Pulaski).

* WHERE...In Georgia, Coastal Bryan, Coastal Chatham, Coastal
Liberty and Coastal McIntosh Counties. In South Carolina,
Beaufort and Coastal Jasper Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 PM this evening to
10 PM EST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 5 AM
to 11 AM EST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Saltwater inundation will impact some roads.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tide will occur around 8 AM Wednesday
morning at Fort Pulaski. Saltwater inundation will be possible
1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Visit water.weather.gov for additional water level and flood
impact information.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 3 to 4 feet above ground level is possible Wednesday along shorelines and low- lying coastal areas. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 3 to 4 feet. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County Coast zones. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 3:15PM PST until November 25 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along
the coast. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 3 to 4 feet above ground level
is possible Wednesday along shorelines and low- lying coastal
areas. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding
possible Thursday with inundation up to 3 to 4 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County
Coast zones.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM PST Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 4 PM PST
Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday
night through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock
people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over
rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.
weather.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays. * SHORELINE IMPACTS...Breaking waves of 3 to 6 ft will result in areas of dune erosion and localized overwashes. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Two to three feet of inundation above ground level expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches. * WHEN...From 5 AM Wednesday to 3 PM EST Friday. * IMPACTS...At this level, flooding may become severe enough to cause structural damage along with widespread roadway flooding in coastal and bayside communities, and near inland tidal waterways. Some locations may become isolated by the flood waters. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal flooding is expected on Wednesday morning. The most severe and impactful high tide will be with Thursday morning's high tide, where major tidal flooding is possible.

location.region: Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 2:30PM EST until November 27 at 3:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Two to three feet of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Wednesday to 3 PM EST Friday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding may become severe enough to
cause structural damage along with widespread roadway flooding
in coastal and bayside communities, and near inland tidal
waterways. Some locations may become isolated by the flood
waters.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor tidal flooding is expected on
Wednesday morning. The most severe and impactful high tide will
be with Thursday morning's high tide, where major tidal
flooding is possible.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that moderate or major tidal
flooding is occurring or imminent. Be prepared for rising water
levels and take appropriate action to protect life and property.
Follow the recommendations of local emergency management
officials.

Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The water may be
deeper than you think it is. You will be putting yourself in
danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to costly
repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
weather.areaDesc: Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...From 7 PM EST this evening through late Wednesday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida, and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated flooding issues across the east coast metro areas. Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case (High-End): 4-6 inches of rain - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 2.4 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet. For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is possible in low- lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast, Northern Monterey Bay and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday night to midnight PST Wednesday night. * WHERE...Low-lying areas along the San Pablo Bay, Carquinez Strait,
and Suisun Bay shorelines in Solano County.

* WHEN...Until 400 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of low-lying areas including parks, lots,
roads, marshes, and vulnerable islands. Erosion along levees is
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 113 PM PST, NWS meteorologists have determined that
abnormally high tides will result in Coastal Flooding.
- The highest tides each day are forecast as follows (all times
local). MHHW is Mean Higher High Water, or the average
highest daily tide; MLLW is Mean Lower Low Water, or the
average lowest daily tide.
* Port Chicago: +2.5 ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 12:16 PM Tue
11/24, +2.6 ft MHHW (7.5 ft MLLW) at 1:01 PM Wed 11/25, +2.5
ft MHHW (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.2 ft MHHW
(7.1 ft MLLW) at 2:45 PM Fri 11/27.
* West Sacramento: +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 3:32 PM Tue
11/24, +2.4 ft MHHW (6.8 ft MLLW) at 4:18 PM Wed 11/25, +2.3
ft MHHW (6.7 ft MLLW) at 5:08 PM Thu 11/26, and +2.1 ft MHHW
(6.5 ft MLLW) at 6:02 PM Fri 11/27.
* Rio Vista (Datum NAVD88): +7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Tue 11/24,
+7.6 ft at 3:00 PM Wed 11/25, +7.5 ft at 4:00 PM Thu 11/26,
+7.4 ft at 5:00 PM Fri 11/27 and +7.0 ft at 6:00 PM Sat
11/28.
- These predictions include up to +1.5 feet of storm surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
Timing of high tide may vary by several hours throughout the
San Francisco Bay and Delta.
- Real-time water levels and latest forecasts are available at:
* Port Chicago: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatidepre
dictions.html?id=9415144
* West Sacramento: https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/noaatide
predictions.html?id=9416131
* Rio Vista: https://water.noaa.gov/gauges/RVBC1
weather.instruction:
Some roads that are commonly dry may become inundated during high
tide. If you encounter flooded roadways: turn around, dont drown.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Sub-freezing temperatures in the mid to upper 20s expected.

* WHERE...All of west central Texas.

* WHEN...From 11 PM this evening to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other

weather.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means sub-freezing temperatures are imminent or
highly likely. These conditions will kill crops and other sensitive
vegetation.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold. To prevent
freezing and possible bursting of outdoor water pipes they should be
wrapped, drained, or allowed to drip slowly. Those that have
in-ground sprinkler systems should drain them and cover above-ground
pipes to protect them from freezing.

events.title: High Surf Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves along the coast. For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding expected. Inundation of 3 to 4 feet above ground level is possible Wednesday along shorelines and low-lying coastal areas. For the Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 3 to 4 feet. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County Coast zones. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 4 PM PST Wednesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through Thursday afternoon. * IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast; Grays Harbor County Coast

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast and Grays Harbor County

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 PM PST Wednesday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 4 PM PST

weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

and Twitter.

events.title: Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected. * WHERE...Northeastern Palm Beach County in southeastern Florida... * WHEN...Until 745 AM EST. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - At 537 AM EST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen. - Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding. - Some locations that will experience flooding include... West Palm Beach, Jupiter, Palm Beach Gardens, Riviera Beach, Palm Beach, Tequesta, Juno Beach, North Palm Beach, Lake Park, Haverhill, Juno Ridge, Port Of Palm Beach, Schall Circle, Downtown West Palm Beach, Lake Belvedere Estates, Golden Lakes, Mangonia Park, Fau North Campus and Lakeside Green. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level

waterways.

weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

repairs.

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County and Metropolitan Miami Dade. * WHEN...Through late tonight. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, 1 1/2 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level expected in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. For the Coastal Flood Watch, 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level possible in vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline. * WHERE...Hudson, Eastern Bergen, Eastern Essex and Eastern Union Counties. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 7 AM Thursday to 6 AM EST Friday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Friday morning through Friday afternoon. * COASTAL FLOOD IMPACTS...Widespread minor to moderate flooding of vulnerable areas near the waterfront and shoreline, including roads, parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes and businesses with basements near the waterfront. Numerous road closures are likely, and vehicles parked in vulnerable areas near the waterfront will likely become flooded. Flooding will also extend inland from the waterfront along tidal rivers and bays, including the tidal portions of the Hackensack River and Passaic Rivers. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The highest water levels are likely with the Thursday morning and evening high tides, potentially extending into the Friday morning high tides. The forecast has been leaned towards a higher end water level scenario to provide a bit of safety margin. If the timing of strongest winds is quicker than currently forecast the peak water level forecast could be increased by a few tenths for Thursday morning. if slower the Thursday morning forecast could be lowered slightly.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 4:10AM AST until November 25 at 6:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
weather.description:
* WHAT...High risk of life-threatening rip currents.

* WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline,
from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In the U.S.
Virgin Islands, along the northern exposed beaches of St.
Thomas, St. John and adjacent islands.

* WHEN...Through this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
weather.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. * WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island Counties. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this evening. For the Coastal Flood Statement, until 6 AM CST early this morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this afternoon. * IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

location.region: Kenedy Island; Willacy Island; Cameron Island

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 2:08AM CST until November 25 at 6:00PM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 3
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Statement,
isolated minor coastal flooding. For the High Rip Current
Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST this
evening. For the Coastal Flood Statement, until 6 AM CST early
this morning. For the High Rip Current Risk, through this
afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Wave run-up may approach the dunes along narrow
beaches. Beach equipment, such as umbrellas and chairs, could
be moved by waves. Vehicles driving along narrow beaches may
experience higher water levels. Elevated water levels may also
occur across the Laguna Madre and South Bay, and along State
Highway 4 west of Boca Chica State Park. Dangerous swimming
and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Do not drive through flooded roadways.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

weather.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 25 at 2:55AM EST until November 27 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents and
rough surf. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal
flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Thursday
night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 11 AM EST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Some flooding of low-lying lots, parks and roadways
may occur near the shoreline. Only isolated road closures are
expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

In Washington, South Washington Coast.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are possible. Travel could be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
weather.instruction:
Fasten loose objects or shelter objects in a safe location prior to
the onset of winds.

Consider sleeping in a location that is furthest away from large
trees and power lines. Be aware of your surroundings and where you
are relative to nearby trees and powerlines.

Prepare for potential power outages. If you have a gas-powered
generator, ensure you have enough fuel. Ensure you have batteries,
flashlights, and a way to maintain a safe body temperature if you
were to lose heating and cooling.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

weather.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and
7 inches.

* WHERE...Portions of east central, northeast, and southeast
Missouri.

* WHEN...From noon today to 6 PM CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Roads, and especially bridges and overpasses, will likely
become slick and hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on

weather.instruction:
Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

events.description: * WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph, with gusts up to 60 mph expected. * WHERE...Northwest Pocahontas, Southeast Randolph, Southeast Webster, and Southeast Nicholas Counties. * WHEN...From 1 AM to 7 PM EST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines. Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

location.region: Southeast Nicholas; Southeast Webster; Northwest Pocahontas; Southeast Randolph

weather.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 25 at 1:59AM EST until November 26 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Charleston WV
weather.description:
* WHAT...East winds 20 to 30 mph, with gusts up to 60 mph expected.

* WHERE...Northwest Pocahontas, Southeast Randolph, Southeast
Webster, and Southeast Nicholas Counties.

* WHEN...From 1 AM to 7 PM EST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds will blow down trees and power lines.
Widespread power outages are expected. Travel will be difficult,
especially for high profile vehicles.
weather.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind.

Remain in the lower levels of your home during the windstorm, and
avoid windows. Watch for falling debris and tree limbs. Use caution
if you must drive.

Additional information can be found at https://www.weather.gov/rlx as
well as on our X and Facebook pages.

sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

weather.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 25 at 1:24AM EST until November 26 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Jacksonville FL
weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 7 feet. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Southeast Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 7 PM EST this
evening. For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 AM EST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides, combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of inundation above ground level Wednesday, with up to 2.6 ft of inundation expected on Thursday. * WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and Reedsport. * WHEN...Until 7 PM PST Thursday. * IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be during the high tide periods in the late morning/early afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides will still be present, which will likely continue inundation impacts. At the Charleston, Oregon tide gauge, high tide is expected to be at 11:35 AM Wednesday, at 12:23 PM Thursday, and at 1:14 PM Friday. Tides look to return to more typical heights over the weekend.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, moderate coastal
flooding. For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip
currents expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Palm Beach County and Coastal Broward County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 7 AM EST
Thursday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 4 AM EST
Wednesday through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
weather.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.
